turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, doctor, I'm here... I mean, my primary care physician strongly suggested I come talk to someone, but really I’m here because for over a year now—going on fourteen months, actually, ever since the Q3 software rollout last year—I’ve been trying to get someone, anyone, to take me seriously. 

I've been a computer support specialist for decades, right? I have my bachelor's degree, I know how these backend systems operate, I understand database architecture. And suddenly they implement this new ticket rotation software, supposedly to 'optimize workflow,' along with these incredibly aggressive security audits. But it's not about workflow. I've been tracking the assignment algorithms, and I know for an absolute fact that they are being used to build a paper trail against me at work. They specifically route the dead-end tickets to my queue—the ones with corrupted data or unresponsive clients that are guaranteed to breach our service level agreements—and then the security audits automatically flag my account for review. 

I've tried to escalate it. I've sat down with management I don't know how many times to explain what's happening, and they just patronize me. They keep pulling up these sanitized system logs, pointing at the screen and saying, 'Look, it's just automated, it's just the new company policy, everyone is subject to the exact same audits.' But I know how to read a log, and I know how a routing algorithm can be tweaked to target a specific employee ID on the backend. It's incredibly frustrating when you have the technical knowledge to see exactly what they're doing, and they just keep smiling and telling you it's standard policy. I just need someone to actually look at the facts of what they're setting me up for.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unyielding belief that workplace systems are being manipulated to target and build a case against them, despite management providing contradictory evidence via system logs.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one was around that other people couldn't hear?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No. No, absolutely not. I mean, I know why you're asking that, I'm not naive. You're trying to figure out if I'm... if I'm hallucinating or losing my grip on reality, but that's exactly what I've been trying to explain to my supervisor, to HR, to anyone who will listen. This isn't in my head. I don't hear voices, I don't see things that aren't there. What I see is data. Hard, quantifiable data. 

I mean, if I were hearing voices, how would that even explain the ticket metrics? You can't hallucinate a server log. You can't imagine a 400% increase in tier-three escalation failures that only happen on my shift, right after a supposedly 'random' security audit locks me out of the admin console for twenty minutes. That's not a voice in my head telling me they're out to get me. That's a timestamped event in the SQL database. I sit in my home office—it's very quiet, actually, I live alone, I have acoustic panels set up because I need absolute focus when I'm debugging—and the only sound I hear is the hum of my cooling fan and the notification ping when another sabotaged ticket drops into my queue. So no, doctor, no voices. Just the very real, very documented sound of my career being systematically dismantled.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that their coworkers or employer are out to get them and systematically dismantling their career through sabotaged tickets.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices or seeing things that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of your work, have you felt that people in your personal life, like family or friends, have also been untrustworthy or working against you?
turns.patient_response:
No, no, not at all. My personal life is... well, it's very separate from all of this. I mean, I don't have a huge circle of friends—never really have, to be honest. I've always been more of an introvert, which is probably why I gravitated toward backend IT work in the first place. You don't need to be a social butterfly to write a good SQL query, you know? And my family, well, my sister lives out in Oregon, we talk maybe once a month, mostly just catching up on her kids, the weather, that sort of thing. She doesn't really understand what I do for a living anyway. If I tried to explain the intricacies of a targeted algorithm to her, her eyes would just glaze over. 

So, no, I don't feel like anyone in my personal life is working against me. Why would they? They don't have access to the company servers. They don't have a vested interest in my performance metrics or my severance package. This is strictly a professional sabotage. It's confined entirely to the corporate network and the management structure there. 

I actually make a very deliberate point to keep my work and my personal life completely compartmentalized. When I log off for the day—assuming I haven't been locked out by one of those 'random' audits—I shut down the work laptop, I put it in the drawer, and I don't look at it. I mean, I still think about it, obviously, because it's incredibly stressful knowing what they're doing to me, but I don't let it bleed into my interactions with my neighbor when we're getting the mail, or the guy at the grocery store. They're just living their lives. They aren't the ones manipulating my ticket queue. It's just the people at work. That's where the focus is, because that's where the data points.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient maintains a fixed, persecutory belief that they are the victim of 'professional sabotage' and that people at work are 'manipulating my ticket queue,' even though they deny these beliefs extend to their personal life.
